Perform the restore into a new database instance rather than overwriting the existing one so you can verify the data safely [1]. Allow roughly ten minutes per hundred gigabytes for the restore, and expect longer if the instance is under load [1]. Verify the restored data before switching traffic and keep the original instance until verification is complete [1]. Calculate the total possible connections as pool size multiplied by maximum instances and compare this against your plan's connection limit [2]. Reduce the per-instance pool size rather than raising the limit, as many small pools can cause exhaustion [2]. Check for queries that keep transactions open across network calls, which commonly leak connections [2]. If you must keep a high instance count, consider using a connection proxy so pooling occurs centrally [2].

This reply was written automatically from our help article "Backups, retention and point-in-time restore" (DOC-DATA-002). If it does not solve your problem, just reply to this message and a member of our support team will pick it up.
